frequency_question: How often do major bipartisan permitting reform bills successfully pass both chambers and get signed into law during periods of divided control?
membership_rule: Includes major legislative pushes explicitly titled or structured around energy permitting reform and infrastructure siting; excludes narrow appropriations riders or non-controversial single-agency fixes.

cases.name: The 2022 Manchin Permitting Reform Proposal (Attached to Continuing Resolution)
The 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act Permitting Provisions (NEPA timeline reforms)
The 2018 Energy and Natural Resources Act Siting Compromise Attempts

coverage_note: 3 named cases representing the modern era of intense polarization over energy corridors and NEPA timelines.
known_gaps: Excludes minor provisions buried in broader defense authorizations that did not feature interstate pipeline siting battles.
skeleton: Three distinct legislative vehicles under divided control where cross-sector permitting reform was explicitly negotiated; 1 success (modest/procedural NEPA changes) vs 2 failures (comprehensive siting/pipeline overhaul).
validity_reason: Valid until the end of the current Congress, after which the baseline resets depending on the composition of the next legislature.
